label: input letter a in the original phase (after a, at t=0, or after certain letters)
explanation: Fires mainly when the input token is a during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. Input a accounts for about 68% of activation mass, but only about 40% of original-phase a inputs fire. Which a inputs fire depends on context. An a at t=0 always fires, weakly. An a right after another a almost always fires, and runs of a ramp up toward the maximum (u u a a a gives 0.59, 0.92, 1.00 of max). An a after certain letters (o, r, c, d, f, j, k, u) usually fires. An a after a digit or after letters like t, x, m, h usually does not. Restricting to these contexts lifts precision from 0.40 to 0.77, but the letter set is fitted empirically. Smaller parts: weak firing on the token right after an a (r, o, c, i), and weak firing at the <DEL> step on 3% of sequences (about 20% of mass), which this predicate does not cover. It is essentially silent in the copy phase and on most other input tokens.
